correctness.rationale: Polar-coordinate first variation gives the stated angular integrand. Odd terms cancel under the half turn; the even forcing integral is twice the integral of a cosine-power primitive over the positive switching semicircle, giving 4 sin^(2j+1)(φ)/(2j+1) before period normalization. The disjoint even and odd monomials give the Descartes bound at fixed tilt. Prescribing p+q+1 distinct positive zeros gives a nonzero coefficient vector; the same bound rules out missing monomials, multiple zeros, or extra positive zeros. For fixed coefficients, simple finite roots persist by the implicit function theorem. A sequence of small roots forces r/s→−B0/A0, and r=su gives a simple limiting equation. A sequence of escaping roots must have sr→∞; comparing the two leading terms rules out q≤p and equal signs, and otherwise forces s^γr→(−A_p/B_q)^(1/d), d=2(q−p)−1, γ=(2q+1)/d. On this scale both lower-degree remainders converge to zero in C¹ near the candidate, ensuring exactly one simple root. Compactness in the extended radius line rules out any others. On a fixed crossing annulus at a fixed positive tilt, composing the two smooth crossing flow segments gives the C¹ first variation of the return map and hence a hyperbolic cycle at each simple zero.

value.rationale: The optimized count at each fixed angle does not say what happens under a small physical tilt without retuning coefficients. The classification answers that question, gives precise radius scales for branches entirely missed by compact-annulus convergence, and identifies which averaged crossings can persist without claiming more uniform cycle existence than proved.
